record_title: Sharp dimension-two counterexamples to q-ary mirror vanishing
provenance: A projective-line multiplicity classification shows exactly when a q-ary [2d+1,2,d] code can have a local gap above d while retaining a full-weight codeword, producing sharp counterexamples to the direct q-ary analogue of a recent binary mirror-vanishing theorem.
limitations: The theorem classifies the extremal dimension-two family with n=2d+1 and a full-weight violating word. It does not classify all q-ary mirror phenomena or identify sufficient hypotheses restoring a q-ary theorem. Folklore and near-simultaneous priority risk remain material because the projective-line proof is short and the motivating binary preprint is recent.
